packs.title: Computing, Coding & AI Thinking
packs.subject: Computing
packs.description: 20 original questions about algorithms, coding concepts, data and thoughtful AI use.

questions.question: What is an algorithm?
options: A sequence of steps to solve a problem
questions.explanation: Algorithms describe ordered steps for completing a task.

questions.question: What does a loop do in a program?
questions.explanation: A loop executes a block multiple times.

questions.question: What does a variable store?
questions.explanation: Variables hold data used by a program.

questions.question: Which symbol is often used for an assignment in many programming languages?
questions.explanation: Many languages use an equals sign to assign a value, though syntax varies.

questions.question: What is a boolean value?
questions.explanation: Boolean logic represents two truth values.

questions.question: What does debugging mean?
questions.explanation: Debugging investigates why code behaves incorrectly.

questions.question: Which data type best represents a person's age in whole years?
questions.explanation: An integer represents a whole number.

questions.question: What is a conditional statement?
options: Code that chooses an action based on a condition
questions.explanation: Conditionals allow different paths based on true or false checks.

questions.question: What is a function in programming?
questions.explanation: Functions group instructions for reuse.

questions.question: What is the purpose of testing software?
options: To check expected and unexpected behaviour
questions.explanation: Tests find regressions and unexpected behaviour before release.

questions.question: What is training data used for in machine learning?
questions.explanation: Training algorithms learn statistical patterns from examples.

questions.question: Why should an AI answer be checked?
options: Every AI answer is a legal document
AI can confidently produce incorrect information
questions.explanation: Model outputs can be inaccurate or fabricated.

questions.question: What is an example of personal data?
questions.explanation: A home address can identify or locate someone.

questions.question: What does encryption help protect?
questions.explanation: Encryption makes data unreadable without the appropriate key.

questions.question: Which approach makes a program easier to maintain?
options: Use clear names and small functions
questions.explanation: Readable modules make software easier to understand and revise.

questions.question: What is a database?
options: A structured system for storing and retrieving data
questions.explanation: Databases organise and query stored information.

questions.question: What is an API?
options: An interface through which software components communicate
questions.explanation: An API defines ways programs request and exchange information.

questions.question: Why is input validation important?
options: It makes all inputs trusted automatically
It checks whether supplied values meet expected rules
questions.explanation: Validation rejects malformed or unacceptable data.

questions.question: What is rate limiting intended to do?
options: Restrict excessive requests to a service
questions.explanation: Rate limiting reduces overload and some forms of abuse.

questions.question: Which is a good way to build safer classroom software?
options: Test permissions using accounts with different roles
Trust any button click as authorization
questions.explanation: Role-separated testing checks that unauthorized users cannot gain access.

packs.title: Real-World Maths: Data & Decisions
packs.subject: Mathematics
packs.description: 20 reasoning-focused word problems about money, charts, measurement and percentage.

questions.question: A notebook costs RM8. You buy three. What is the total cost?
questions.explanation: Three notebooks cost 3 × RM8 = RM24.

questions.question: A bus has 42 passengers. 15 get off. How many remain?
questions.explanation: 42 − 15 = 27 passengers.

questions.question: A class of 30 students has 18 girls. What fraction of the class is girls in simplest form?
questions.explanation: 18/30 simplifies to 3/5.

questions.question: A shop reduces RM50 by 10%. What is the new price?
questions.explanation: 10% of RM50 is RM5; RM50 − RM5 = RM45.

questions.question: A rectangle is 8 cm long and 5 cm wide. What is its area?
questions.explanation: Area equals length × width = 8 × 5 = 40 cm².

questions.question: A 2-litre bottle is shared equally into four cups. How much is in each cup?
Six test scores are 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10. What is their mean?
questions.explanation: The sum is 45; the mean is 45 ÷ 6 = 7.5.

questions.question: A cyclist rides 12 km in one hour at a steady speed. How far in 3 hours?
questions.explanation: Distance is 12 × 3 = 36 km.

questions.question: What is 0.75 as a fraction in simplest form?
questions.explanation: 0.75 equals 75/100, which simplifies to 3/4.

questions.question: A bag contains 4 red and 6 blue marbles. What is the probability of picking red?
questions.explanation: 4 out of 10 marbles are red, so 4/10 = 2/5.

questions.question: What is the perimeter of a square with side 7 cm?
questions.explanation: Four sides of 7 cm give 4 × 7 = 28 cm.

questions.question: A recipe uses 200 g of flour for 4 muffins. How much flour for 10 muffins at the same rate?
questions.explanation: Each muffin needs 50 g; 10 need 500 g.

questions.question: What is the next number in 4, 9, 14, 19, ...?
questions.explanation: Each term increases by 5.

questions.question: A train leaves at 14:20 and arrives at 15:05. How long is the journey?
questions.explanation: From 14:20 to 15:00 is 40 min, plus 5 min.

questions.question: If 25% of a class is absent and the class has 32 students, how many are absent?
questions.explanation: 25% is one quarter; 32 ÷ 4 = 8.

questions.question: A box holds 12 pencils. How many boxes are needed for 70 pencils?
questions.explanation: Five boxes hold only 60; six hold 72.

questions.question: What is 3/8 + 2/8?
questions.explanation: Add numerators when denominators match: 3/8 + 2/8 = 5/8.

questions.question: A tank has 18 L, and 2.5 L is used. How much remains?
A map uses 1 cm to represent 5 km. How far is 4 cm on the map?
The prices RM7, RM9, RM11, RM13, RM15 are recorded. What is their median?
questions.explanation: The middle value of the five sorted prices is RM11.
